CanBeGeneratedByModifiers.rationale: `=> false` (BadLuck.cs:13) == the class attribute; Bad Luck is therefore excluded from the random-curse pool on both sides.

MaxUpgradeLevel.rationale: `=> 0` (BadLuck.cs:15) == the class attribute, so `is_upgradable` is False and Apotheosis/Armaments skip it on both sides.

CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ Eternal, Unplayable }` (BadLuck.cs:17-21) == `eternal` + `is_playable = False`. NOT Ethereal (unlike AscendersBane), and the sim correctly leaves `is_ethereal` at its False default.

HasTurnEndInHandEffect.rationale: `public override bool HasTurnEndInHandEffect => true` (BadLuck.cs:23) == the class attribute (cards/base.py:63), the flag the end-of-turn hand pass consults before calling OnTurnEndInHand.

ctor.issue: Type/rarity/target map exactly (CURSE / CURSE / NONE), but the canonical energy cost is **-1** in C# (`base(-1, ...)`, BadLuck.cs:27-30) and **0** in the sim (`self._energy_cost = 0`, bad_luck.py:34). Same divergence as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry and, per rule 3, the same verdict: `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), making the game's unplayable curse immune to every cost modifier, while the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain in `Card.energy_cost` (cards/base.py:222-232). DORMANT for the same executed reason -- the three ported cost readers (`relics/mummified_hand.py:25` and `potions.py:168` filter `> 0`; `cards/event_cards.py:328` skips `<= 1`) and the one pool filter (`events/infested_automaton.py:35`, over `pool_card_ids()`, which holds no curses) all treat -1 and 0 alike. Live as soon as any effect reads an unplayable card's cost without a `> 0` filter.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: nothing -- the sim inlines 13 at the damage site (bad_luck.py:43)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new HpLossVar(13m)` (BadLuck.cs:25) is a printed card var; the sim declares no `_hp_loss` in `_init_vars`, so `Card.base_hp_loss` (cards/base.py:202-210) returns its 0 default for this card and the number 13 exists only as a literal inside `on_turn_end_in_hand`. The DEALT damage is identical (13 either way), so no player-visible combat outcome differs -- but the sim's own printed-number API misreports the card, and it is read: `full_env.py:488` encodes `card.base_hp_loss / ABS_SCALE` into the observation vector, so a policy sees Bad Luck as a harmless 0-HP-loss curse. Recorded as a gap rather than a deliberate divergence because nothing in the code marks it intentional and every other numbered card in this batch does declare its var. DORMANT with respect to game fidelity (no game-observable difference); LIVE with respect to the sim's observation encoder. The concrete fix is a one-line `self._hp_loss = 13` in `_init_vars` -- NOT applied, per the no-engine-edits rule.

OnTurnEndInHand.rationale: `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.HpLoss.BaseValue, ValueProp.Unblockable | ValueProp.Unpowered | ValueProp.Move, this)` (BadLuck.cs:35) == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, 13, card=self, props=DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS)`. `DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS` is exactly `UNBLOCKABLE | UNPOWERED | MOVE` (valueprops.py:38). Self-targeted, and both sides pass no dealer (C# omits the dealer argument entirely, the sim leaves `dealer` at its None default), so no AfterDamageGiven attribution fires on either side. Presentation, folded in: BadLuck.cs:34 awaits Cmd.Wait(0.25f) before the damage -- pacing only.

OnPlay.rationale: BadLuck.cs declares no OnPlay; the card is Unplayable. The sim's abstract method is satisfied with a `pass`.

guards.what: the damage is UNBLOCKABLE, so block never absorbs it, and UNPOWERED, so Strength/Vulnerable/Weak never scale it
guards.rationale: `is_powered_attack` is `MOVE in props and UNPOWERED not in props` (valueprops.py:49), which is False here on both sides; and the UNBLOCKABLE branch of the sim's damage pipeline skips block exactly as C#'s does. The MOVE bit is still set on both sides, so effects keyed on 'card or monster move' (Vambrace's `IsCardOrMonsterMove()`) see it identically.
